steps.statement: On wkstn-07, winword.exe spawned cmd.exe (EVT-0221), and two seconds later cmd.exe spawned powershell.exe (pid 5104) under user jdavis at 2026-06-10T08:12:35.000000Z with the command line 'powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc JABjAGwAaQBlAG4AdA...' — a document-application-to-shell chain ending in a hidden, base64-encoded PowerShell payload.

Endpoint event EVT-0222 records a process named powershell.exe (obs_f7510556968d) whose parent process is cmd.exe (obs_0ef69125c19a), i.e. PowerShell launched from a command shell rather than interactively from a shell UI. The cited observations carry no hostname, username, command line or pid, so neither the executing host/account nor what PowerShell ran is established here; an EVT-0222 field for hostname/username/command_line, or a PowerShell script-block/module logging record for the same execution, would be needed to close that gap. The nearest temporally related records are the EVT-0209 cloud_storage fields at 2026-06-10T08:50:44.249433Z (obs_c17ec95f8881) under username 'dtaylor' (obs_efc3a4318676) from source_ip 10.0.2.17 (obs_50462666fe77), 2289.249433 seconds away, a separation of roughly 38 minutes that does not by itself link the shell activity to that cloud access.

The nearest endpoint activity in time to the outbound flow EVT-0223 to 185.220.101.45 (obs_8ca591c0ba53) is EVT-0150, 143.279231 seconds away, on host wkstn-05 under username dtaylor: word.exe (pid 5002, process_path 'microsoft', integrity_level 'medium') spawned by parent teams.exe at 2026-06-10T09:05:40.279231Z. EVT-0223, EVT-0224 and EVT-0225 carry only the destination address 185.220.101.45 and no source host, user or process field, so this temporal adjacency does not attribute the traffic to wkstn-05 or dtaylor; a network record bearing a source host/process, or a process-to-connection correlation on wkstn-05, would be needed to close that gap.

Network event EVT-0225, a flow to 185.220.101.45, carries source attribution absent from the anchor: src_host 'wkstn-07' (obs_b791737b5e85) with src_ip 10.0.2.47 (obs_4736dae95664), over tcp (obs_e2f473d4b9dd) to dst_port 443 (obs_ffbd322e2775) at 2026-06-10T09:34:21.000000Z (obs_07db70cbe0c7), sending 987 bytes and receiving 3201 bytes (obs_aeb0730cd5c1, obs_e902ea8816c8); it shares the destination address 185.220.101.45 with EVT-0224 (obs_a9eb81b4cb9c) 937 seconds earlier, tying that repeated outbound contact to wkstn-07.

Three distinct network events, EVT-0223 (obs_8ca591c0ba53), EVT-0224 (obs_a9eb81b4cb9c) and EVT-0225 (obs_4714251c0355), all record a destination address of 185.220.101.45, indicating repeated outbound contact with a single external endpoint. None of the cited observations carries a source host, user or process field, so no endpoint or account is tied to this traffic; a network record bearing a source host/process attribution, or a process-to-connection correlation on the originating host, would be needed to establish that link.

Endpoint event EVT-0230 records execution of net.exe (obs_2ac0a28281d4), the built-in network/share and account enumeration utility. The cited observations for EVT-0230 carry no hostname, username, command line, pid or parent process, so neither the executing host/account nor the subcommand is established here; an EVT-0230 field for hostname/username/command_line, or a process-creation record from the same host's endpoint agent, would be needed to close that gap. Its nearest temporally related records are the EVT-0110 network fields at 2026-06-10T11:33:38.176114Z (obs_7c58a54a78ef) for a tcp (obs_0609d699aad4) flow from src_ip 10.0.1.13 (obs_1bfa12e5f29b) to dst_ip 10.0.5.19 (obs_3d50340fd98d) on dst_port 53 (obs_70040b6134b9) with bytes_sent 48795 (obs_d8c377fb6985) and bytes_recv 137177 (obs_e38985573038), action 'allowed' (obs_46ca7e384646), 296.176114 seconds away — a separation of roughly five minutes that does not by itself tie the net.exe execution to that flow, and no observation cited here names a host or process for either the 10.0.1.13 or 10.0.5.19 side.

The single dst_port 445 network event EVT-0231 (obs_dd24d4929cd4) precedes by 31 seconds the installation of service 'psexesvc' with service_path 'psexesvc.exe' on host file-srv-02 under username jdavis at 2026-06-10T13:12:04.000000Z (EVT-0232: obs_184b3dbaace7, obs_60a53547af4a, obs_7d30c81f008c, obs_fe4a928be14f, obs_9f81d2d1d113), and by 34 seconds the follow-on EVT-0233 activity on the same host file-srv-02 under the same username jdavis at 2026-06-10T13:12:07.000000Z (obs_9c45b5c6189a, obs_f552866366ac, obs_42ead5b62ef2) — the pattern of SMB admin-share access followed by PsExec service creation and execution. EVT-0231 carries only dst_port 445 among the cited observations, with no source or destination host, user or process field, so the SMB flow is not attributed to file-srv-02 or jdavis by these records; a network record bearing src_host/dst_host or a source process, or an authentication log for the 445 session on file-srv-02, would be required to close that gap.

Endpoint event EVT-0233 records a process named cmd.exe (obs_44ba24f843ab), a command shell. The cited EVT-0233 observation carries no hostname, username, command line, pid or parent process, so neither the executing host/account nor what the shell ran is established here; an EVT-0233 hostname/username/command_line field, or a process-creation record from the same host's endpoint agent, would be needed to attribute it. Its nearest temporally related records are the EVT-0187 endpoint fields at 2026-06-10T13:40:10.848419Z (obs_0c0777d0de45) for word.exe (obs_17c320943d11) spawned by explorer.exe (obs_0b8c629840a8), pid 4090 (obs_bcb38cbba3e0), integrity_level 'medium' (obs_50895533f5de), process_path 'microsoft' (obs_a6023415d341), under username asmith (obs_4bc6676c461d) on hostname wkstn-02 (obs_b10ca951ffa0), 1683.848419 seconds away — roughly twenty-eight minutes, and an interactively launched document application rather than a shell parent, so it does not by itself place EVT-0233 on wkstn-02 or under asmith.

Endpoint event EVT-0233 records cmd.exe (obs_44ba24f843ab) spawned by parent process psexesvc.exe (obs_cb87031c57b2), the service-side component of PsExec, indicating a command shell launched via remote service execution rather than by a local interactive shell. The cited observations carry no hostname or username, so the executing host and account are not established here; an EVT-0233 record field for hostname/username, or an authentication/service-install log for the same event, would be needed to close that gap.

Endpoint event EVT-0234 records net.exe (obs_9db3c9019c41) spawned by parent process cmd.exe (obs_27f847ad5fdf) — the built-in network/share and account enumeration utility run from a command shell. It sits 153 seconds from endpoint event EVT-0235 at 2026-06-10T14:07:55.000000Z (obs_8163e55a7811) on hostname file-srv-02 (obs_f01f881129ba) under username jdavis (obs_618ee48830b3), where cmd.exe (obs_59f1be1fe4fa, pid 4044 obs_ee39ef851987) ran command_line 'dir /s /b \\FILE-SRV-02\finance-data' (obs_fefbda991563), so the two form a short burst of shell-driven enumeration. The EVT-0234 observations cited carry no hostname, username, command line or pid, so the net.exe invocation is not itself attributed to file-srv-02 or jdavis and its subcommand is unknown; an EVT-0234 field for hostname/username/command_line, or a process-creation record from the same host's endpoint agent, would be needed to close that gap.

Endpoint event EVT-0235 records a process named cmd.exe (obs_59f1be1fe4fa) whose parent process is itself cmd.exe (obs_0a1c4d0a7b95), i.e. a nested command shell spawned from another command shell. The cited observations carry no hostname, username, command line or pid, so neither the executing host/account nor what the shell ran is established here; an EVT-0235 field for hostname/username/command_line, or a matching process-creation record from the host's endpoint agent, would be needed to close that gap. An endpoint file event (EVT-0237) and a cloud_storage event (EVT-0238) both record a file_size_bytes of 2473829122, consistent with a single ~2.47 GB object staged on the endpoint and then present in cloud storage. Neither cited observation carries a user, host or destination account field here, so the actor and target account are not established; an endpoint file record with a path/user attribution or a cloud_storage record with an uploading principal would be needed to close that gap.

The 2,473,829,122-byte cloud_storage event EVT-0238 (obs_6861e8f4de91) shares its size with endpoint file event EVT-0237 (obs_3dfc08d5bf03), but the nearest endpoint activity in time, 24.876335 seconds away, is EVT-0159 on host wkstn-01 under user jclark: teams.exe (pid 1052, process_path 'microsoft', integrity_level 'medium') started by parent explorer.exe at 2026-06-10T18:19:08.876335Z, which carries no file-size or transfer field tying it to the 2,473,829,122-byte object. Temporal adjacency alone therefore attributes the transfer to no host or account; an endpoint file or network record bearing both the size 2473829122 and a username/hostname, or a cloud_storage record naming an uploading principal, would be required.
